notes: §1985:XIII.4.2.3 SR2: 'The availability of the phrases within the CLOSE statement is dependent on the level of Sequential I-O module supported by the implementation.' WiseOwl supports the level-2 Sequential I-O CLOSE at every edition: the grammar's closeOption takes REEL/UNIT [FOR] REMOVAL, WITH NO REWIND and WITH LOCK (the double-barred level-2 elements of §1985:VII.4.2.2) and SequentialIoBinder#BindClose admits a report file (admitsReportFile) and maps each written form to its BoundCloseKind, so every RW CLOSE phrase is available at --std 85. Probes at --std 85: class e (sequential report file, each phrase) plain, WITH LOCK, LOCK, WITH NO REWIND, REEL, UNIT FOR REMOVAL, REEL REMOVAL all compile and run (CLOSED); class b refusals REEL WITH LOCK and WITH LOCK NO REWIND (two phrases) COBOL2269, bare CLOSE. COBOL0001, CLOSE f WITH. COBOL5506; class e after a failed state, CLOSE of an unopened file and a second CLOSE both set FS=42 and continue. Class c: no 2002+ CLOSE phrase exists to refuse; classes a, d, f do not apply. The witness closes two report files WITH LOCK / WITH NO REWIND and prints CLOSED.

next.reason: 1985: "The availability of the phrases within the CLOSE statement is dependent on the level of Sequential I-O module supported"; 2023: "No modules or levels; SR-14.9.6.3-1 restricts the NO REWIND, REEL, UNIT phrases only to sequential files, with no level dependence". 2023 has no module levels. The CLOSE phrases are limited only by file organization (SR-14.9.6.3-1), so the level-dependent availability rule is dropped.
